content.title: About
content.content: Eggplant is a nightshade vegetable native to South Asia. When cooked without added fat, it retains a tender flavor, low calorie count, and a rich supply of vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggplant contains antioxidant compounds such as nasunin that help protect cells from oxidative stress.
In different cultures the vegetable has various names: in Japan it is called “nasu,” in Italy “melanzana.”
There are more than 500 cultivars of eggplant, varying in shape, color, and size.
Its porous flesh makes eggplant an excellent vehicle for sauces in many dishes.
Ancient Roman recipes featured eggplant cooked with honey and spices.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: 100 g of eggplant cooked without fat provides about 20 kcal, making it a great choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain healthy blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggplant supplies vitamin B6, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Nasunin and anthocyanins combat free radicals, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Potassium, magnesium, and copper in eggplant contribute to blood‑pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggplant, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Eggplant contains oxalates, which in high amounts can increase the risk of kidney‑stone formation.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with many vegetables, eggplant may carry pesticide residues; washing thoroughly or choosing organic is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eggplant without added fat can be steamed, baked, stewed, or microwaved. Slice it into cubes, rounds, or puree it for soups, ragouts, and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store eggplant in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a paper towel, for up to 5–7 days. Keep it away from ethylene‑producing fruits.
